solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Place starts heaving — it's set after a break?

indicators.note: heaving suggests things being thrown about, so the letters of the two words before are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A town's opening stages are in turmoil, as if something is being set right after a rupture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place starts' looks like the beginning of a place; it is the fodder, rearranged by 'heaving'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid plaster casing is moulded round a broken limb and hardens so the bone can knit.

clue.text: Friend assumes right in Spain to get confection

indicators.note: assumes means takes on or takes in, so the friend word holds the letter for right

parts.note: a pal is a friend
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A friend takes on a right in Spain to obtain a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet made of nuts cooked in boiling sugar, often ground for chocolate fillings.

clue.text: Losing head, go on annoying joint

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to rankle is to go on causing annoyance or resentment

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper and carrying on being irritating, like a sore joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint linking the foot to the leg is one of the body's main joints.

clue.text: Cut for elite sporting group?

definitions.meaning: a cut of beef from the upper hindquarter, usually roasted
read as ..., the leading team in a league

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: a side is a sports team, and the top one is the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's joint from the leg of beef, and, read in two parts, the best team in a competition.

clue.text: Favour group in repetitive ritual

indicators.note: in places the word for group inside the word for the ritual

parts.note: rote is mechanical repetition, a routine done by habit
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A preference for a gang within some tedious routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favour' looks like a verb; here it is the noun, a ribbon badge worn to show support.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour in the old sense is a knot of ribbon worn as a badge, as a rosette is.

clue.text: Australia trip quietly put off yet to be arranged in spartan state

indicators.note: to be arranged means the letters remain to be sorted into order
put off means removed, so the soft letter is taken out of trip

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quietly

explanation.surface: An Australian journey is postponed and still unplanned, in a frugal spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quietly put off' removes P from TRIP, leaving TRI; 'to be arranged' rearranges TRI with YET to make TERITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition of severe simplicity and lack of comfort, the plainness of Sparta.

clue.text: Slight on geek falling short? Painter could need one

parts.note: slight means thin or slender

indicators.note: falling short means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: a nerd is a geek

explanation.surface: A thin swot comes up short, and an artist might need what he has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' in the definition stands for a liquid used to dilute paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A solvent such as white spirit used to dilute paint, which a decorator may need.

clue.text: Expert at university gets to go to pieces

parts.note: a crack shot or crack player is an expert one
up means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A specialist on campus manages to fall apart under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: UP for 'at university' is a British usage: students go up to university and come down at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's composure entirely or have a breakdown is a colloquial phrasal verb meaning fall apart.

clue.text: Alas October is disastrous for cheap domestic disposal

indicators.note: disastrous means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Woe: the autumn month has been a calamity for a household clear-out on the cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: A boot is British for a car's trunk; at such sales people sell unwanted goods from them in a field or car park.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting rid of unwanted household goods at low prices from one's car is the British car-park sale.

clue.text: More impertinent fool that is interrupting senior

indicators.note: interrupting puts the pieces in between the letters of the abbreviation for senior

parts.note: an ass is a fool
i.e. (id est) is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A cheekier idiot butts in on an elder.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of sassy, which is an informal word for cheeky or insolent.

clue.text: Inexperienced person on ship before retreat overturned oil, say

parts.note: raw means green or inexperienced
a mate is a ship's officer

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lair is a retreat or den

explanation.surface: A rookie on board ship comes before a hideaway tipped up by oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is an example of an unprocessed substance used as a basis for manufacture.

clue.text: Breed flat-bodied fish by the sound of it

indicators.note: signals that the word for the fish is to be heard, not written

parts.note: rays are flat-bodied cartilaginous fish such as skates and mantas

explanation.surface: An instruction to breed some flatfish, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear animals or bring up children is a common verb sense of breed.

clue.text: Hint resolved ending in one retired person who's studious being aware

indicators.note: resolved means broken down and reworked, so the letters of Hint are rearranged
ending in takes only the final letter of the word one
retired means drawn back, so the word for the studious person is read backwards

parts.note: a wonk is a studious or bookish person, a swot

explanation.surface: A clue is worked out, with someone bookish who has withdrawn realising what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: A wonk is chiefly an American word for a swot; 'being' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in possession of inside information or current knowledge is an idiom for being well informed.

clue.text: Some no-hoper at engineering work

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hopeless case taking an engineering course gets some work done.
explanation.definitionFit: To function or run, as a machine does, is a straightforward synonym of work as a verb.

clue.text: A loving sound remains reportedly as element in a concert hall?

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: A, then coo (a loving sound), then sticks (remains or stays): spoken together they give the answer

explanation.surface: A tender sound stays on, it is said, as part of a concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The way sound carries in a room is a key property of any concert hall.

clue.text: Rite developed during period in country

indicators.note: during places the rearranged letters within the word for a period

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: developed means changed or worked into another form, so the letters of Rite are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ceremony evolved over an age within some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' makes RIT E from Rite, placed between E and RA of ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation in the Horn of Africa on the Red Sea coast, independent from Ethiopia since 1993.

clue.text: Height many recalled in Caribbean island

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or height, especially on Dartmoor

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the phrase for many is read backwards

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: A tall hill and a crowd are remembered on a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the British Virgin Islands in the Caribbean, the largest of the group.

clue.text: Danger shown by guide commonly in US tree

parts.note: a rock is a danger to shipping

indicators.note: commonly means in common speech, which drops the initial H

parts.note: the helm is what steers or guides a vessel

explanation.surface: A hazard indicated by a guide in plain speech, in an American tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' signals dropping the aitch, as in Cockney speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American species of elm with hard, heavy timber.

clue.text: Land around river is acceptable

indicators.note: around means the word for land goes round the letter for river

parts.note: to alight is to land, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Territory surrounding a river is satisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of all right, meaning satisfactory or good enough.

clue.text: Put up piece of poetry as subject of elevated appreciation?

parts.note: to sky something is to hit or throw it high up, as a cricketer skies a ball
a line is a single piece of a poem

explanation.surface: A verse is offered up as a lofty object of admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' suggests high-minded praise but means viewed from up high.
explanation.definitionFit: A city's outline of rooftops and towers is something people admire from high viewpoints.

clue.text: Additional note about comic novelist in heavy spot

indicators.note: about means turned about, so the abbreviation for the added note is read backwards

parts.note: PS (postscript) is a note added at the end of a letter
David Lodge is an English novelist known for comic campus novels

explanation.surface: A postscript about a funny author, written in a big blot.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, irregular blob or blot of ink or paint, a heavy mark.

clue.text: Understanding within reach?

definitions.meaning: deep perception or comprehension of something
read as ..., close enough to be seen and nearly attained

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into in sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Perception into something's true nature, and, split into two words, the state of being nearly attained.

clue.text: Time in New York artist is among warring clan regarding forebears

indicators.note: is among places the pieces in the middle of the rearranged letters
warring means in conflict, so the letters of clan are thrown into disorder

parts.note: EST is Eastern Standard Time, the time zone of New York
RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: A New York painter finds himself in the middle of a feuding family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is among' places the time and artist letters inside the rearranged clan, after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to one's ancestors, the people from whom one descends, is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Scholars attended by fine African tribe

parts.note: MAs are holders of a Master of Arts degree, so scholars
A1 means first-rate or fine; the 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Academics are accompanied by a splendid group of Africans.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania, also spelt Maasai.

clue.text: Island with pep producing fruit

parts.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
go means energy or pep

explanation.surface: An island full of energy yields fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical stone fruit with sweet orange flesh.

clue.text: Decreasing time for supper?

definitions.meaning: read as de-creasing, removing creases, that is smoothing or levelling
the later part of the day, when supper is eaten

explanation.walkthrough: 'Decreasing' looks like getting smaller; split it as de-creasing to see the smoothing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Making flat or level takes out wrinkles, and the hours after afternoon are the usual mealtime for supper.

clue.text: Completed festivity almost in part of Ireland

parts.note: done means completed or finished

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped from the word for a festivity

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion

explanation.surface: Finished with a near-celebration somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A county in the far north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Single woman with hat to be replaced gets to lose an opportunity

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried woman

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different place, so the letters of the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman whose hat needs swapping loses her chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' reads as part of 'to be replaced' but belongs to the fodder: 'hat to be' is rearranged by 'replaced'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for failing to take advantage of a chance before it has gone.
